T1.implementation_approach: Create a clean and intuitive UI using a frontend framework like React, ensuring easy navigation and search functionality.
T1.notes: Focus on responsive design for different screen sizes.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs to handle problem data retrieval, creation, and updates using a backend framework like Node.js or Django.
T2.notes: Ensure proper authentication and authorization mechanisms.

T3.implementation_approach: Design a relational database schema to store problem details, tags, and metadata using MySQL or PostgreSQL.
T3.notes: Optimize for query performance and scalability.

T4.implementation_approach: Build a user-friendly interface for code submission with syntax highlighting and file upload support.
T4.notes: Integrate with the backend for real-time feedback.

T5.implementation_approach: Develop a backend service to handle code execution and evaluation securely using containerized environments.
T5.notes: Implement timeout and resource usage limits to prevent abuse.

T6.implementation_approach: Set up isolated Docker containers or a sandbox environment to execute user-submitted code safely.
T6.notes: Ensure proper security measures to prevent malicious code execution.

T7.implementation_approach: Design a profile UI to display user details, progress, and achievements using a frontend framework.
T7.notes: Incorporate visual elements like progress bars and badges.

T8.implementation_approach: Develop backend APIs to manage user data, including profile updates and progress tracking.
T8.notes: Ensure data consistency and secure storage of sensitive information.

T9.implementation_approach: Set up a database to store user information, progress, and activity logs using a relational or NoSQL database.

T10.implementation_approach: Create a dynamic leaderboard UI to display top users based on various metrics like scores or activity.
T10.notes: Include filters and sorting options for better usability.

T11.implementation_approach: Implement backend logic to calculate and update leaderboard rankings in real-time or at regular intervals.
T11.notes: Optimize for performance with caching mechanisms.

T12.implementation_approach: Design a UI to display hints and explanations for problems, ensuring they are accessible but not intrusive.
T12.notes: Allow users to toggle visibility of hints.

T13.implementation_approach: Develop backend APIs to manage hints and explanations, including retrieval and updates.
T13.notes: Ensure hints are tied to specific problems in the database.

T14.implementation_approach: Perform end-to-end testing of the problem library, including UI, backend, and database interactions.
T14.notes: Use automated test cases for consistent validation.

T15.implementation_approach: Test the code submission and evaluation flow, including edge cases and security vulnerabilities.
T15.notes: Simulate various user inputs to ensure robustness.

T16.implementation_approach: Validate user profile functionality, including progress tracking and data updates, through manual and automated tests.
T16.notes: Check for data consistency across the system.

T17.implementation_approach: Test the leaderboard functionality for accuracy, performance, and real-time updates.
T17.notes: Verify sorting and filtering options work as expected.

T18.implementation_approach: Test the hints and explanations feature for proper integration with the UI and backend.
T18.notes: Ensure hints are displayed correctly and tied to the right problems.

# app/database.py
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

# Database configuration
DATABASE_URL = "sqlite:///./acm_platform.db"  # Replace with your database URL

# SQLAlchemy Base and engine
engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL, connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
SessionLocal = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine)
Base = declarative_base()

# Dependency to get a database session
def get_db():
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

# app/models/problem.py

from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, String, Text, Boolean
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base

Base = declarative_base()

class Problem(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'
    
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    title = Column(String(255), nullable=False)
    description = Column(Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = Column(String(50), nullable=False)  # e.g., "Easy", "Medium", "Hard"
    is_active = Column(Boolean, default=True)  # Whether the problem is active or not
    
    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Problem(id={self.id}, title={self.title}, difficulty={self.difficulty}, is_active={self.is_active})>"

# app/models/user.py

from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, String, Boolean
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base

Base = declarative_base()

class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = Column(String(50), nullable=False, unique=True)
    email = Column(String(100), nullable=False, unique=True)
    password_hash = Column(String(128), nullable=False)
    is_active = Column(Boolean, default=True)
    is_admin = Column(Boolean, default=False)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<User(username='{self.username}', email='{self.email}', is_active={self.is_active}, is_admin={self.is_admin})>"

from flask import Flask
from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Initialize the database instance
db = SQLAlchemy()

def create_app():
    # Create the Flask application
    app = Flask(__name__, template_folder='../templates', static_folder='../static', static_url_path='/static')
    
    # Configure the application
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///app.db'
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False
    
    # Initialize database
    db.init_app(app)
    
    # Register blueprints here
    # Example: app.register_blueprint(problem_bp)
    
    return app

# Must Export
__all__ = ['db', 'create_app']

from flask import Flask
from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy
from flask_migrate import Migrate

# Initialize the Flask app
app = Flask(__name__)

# Configuration for SQLAlchemy
app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///app.db'
app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False

# Initialize SQLAlchemy and Migrate
db = SQLAlchemy(app)
migrate = Migrate(app, db)

# Import and register blueprints
from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_bp
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_bp

app.register_blueprint(problem_bp)
app.register_blueprint(user_bp)

# Application entry point
if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run(debug=True)

from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base

Base = declarative_base()

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.Enum('Easy', 'Medium', 'Hard', name='difficulty_levels'), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now(), nullable=False)
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now(), nullable=False)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<Problem {self.id} - {self.title}>'

from flask_migrate import Migrate
from app.database import db

migrate = Migrate()

def init_migrate(app):
    migrate.init_app(app, db)

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.current_timestamp())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=True, onupdate=db.func.current_timestamp())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Problem {self.title}>"

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('problems.id'), nullable=False)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, nullable=False)  # Assuming a user table exists
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    language = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.current_timestamp())

    problem = db.relationship('Problem', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Solution {self.id} for Problem {self.problem_id}>"

from sqlalchemy.orm.exc import NoResultFound
from app.database import db

def get_record_by_id(model_class, record_id):
    """
    Retrieve a record by its ID from the database.

    :param model_class: SQLAlchemy model class to query.
    :param record_id: ID of the record to retrieve.
    :return: Record object if found, None otherwise.
    """
    try:
        return db.session.query(model_class).filter_by(id=record_id).one()
    except NoResultFound:
        return None

def add_record(record):
    """
    Add a new record to the database.

    :param record: SQLAlchemy model instance to add.
    """
    db.session.add(record)
    db.session.commit()

def update_record():
    """
    Commit any pending updates to the database.
    """
    db.session.commit()

def delete_record(record):
    """
    Delete a record from the database.

    :param record: SQLAlchemy model instance to delete.
    """
    db.session.delete(record)
    db.session.commit()

def get_records(model_class, filters=None):
    """
    Retrieve multiple records from the database with optional filters.

    :param model_class: SQLAlchemy model class to query.
    :param filters: Optional dictionary of filters to apply.
    :return: List of records.
    """
    query = db.session.query(model_class)
    if filters:
        query = query.filter_by(**filters)
    return query.all()

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

db = SQLAlchemy()

# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM-style programming problems and improve their coding skills.

## Features

- Problem Library: A comprehensive library of ACM-style programming problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Submission and Evaluation: Allows users to submit code solutions and receive instant feedback on correctness and performance.
- User Profiles and Progress Tracking: Enables users to create profiles, track their progress, and view their problem-solving history.
- Leaderboard: Displays rankings of users based on their problem-solving performance and achievements.
- Hints and Explanations: Provides hints and detailed explanations for problems to help users learn and improve.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
